title: A tiger’s fare, a snake’s fare
odia:
ଥିଲେ ବାଘର ଆହାର
ନଥିଲେ ସାପର ଆହାର।
literal_meaning: When there is [food], a tiger’s fare; when there is none, a snake’s fare.
meaning_odia: ଖାଦ୍ୟ ଥିଲେ ପ୍ରଚୁର ଖାଇବା, ନଥିଲେ ଅଭାବରେ ରହିବା—ଏହି ଦୁଇ ଅବସ୍ଥାର ତୁଳନା। ବାଘର ଆହାର ଓ ସାପର ଆହାରର ବିପରୀତ ଚିତ୍ରରେ ପ୍ରଚୁରତାରୁ ଅଭାବକୁ ହୋଇଥିବା ପରିବର୍ତ୍ତନ ଫୁଟିଛି।
explanation: The saying contrasts plentiful eating when food is available with scarcity when it is not. The change from a tiger’s fare to a snake’s fare marks the change in circumstances.
usage_example: Original imagined example: A household uses its food stores freely when they are full and later has very little left. Someone recalls the contrast between fare in plenty and fare in scarcity.
cultural_context: The paired ଥିଲେ and ନଥିଲେ give the contrast its compact form: availability on one side, absence on the other.

witnesses.locator: Page23, sixth item beginning ଥିଲେ ବାଘର ଆହାର.
witnesses.note: Exact uploaded wording and line break retained. Food availability is a contextual reading; the precise nuance of ସାପର ଆହାର remains uncertain.

witnesses.locator: Paragraph discussing Pusha harvest, consumption and saving; line185 in inspected digital text.
witnesses.note: Related expression: ଥିଲେ ବାଘର ଆହାର ନଥିଲେ ପବନ ଆହାର । Public ପବନ differs from upload ସାପର. Article supplies abundance/shortage context, not exact uploaded second-clause attestation.

origin_note: Upload supplies the tiger/snake wording. Samadhwani supplies a related tiger/air expression in a stated food-availability context. Earliest origin and shared lineage unknown.
